get.summary:
JSON build provenance: `version` + `git_sha` + `git_dirty` +
`uptime_seconds`. Same provenance triple the `dynograph_build_info`
gauge surfaces in `/metrics`, JSON-shaped for callers that don't
want to parse Prometheus text format. Public; same auth/middleware
posture as `/metrics`.

Prometheus text-format scrape endpoint. Public — sit alongside
`/health` and `/ready`; the assumption is that the network/
ingress layer gates Prometheus scrape access to the metrics
endpoint when needed (k8s NetworkPolicy / Caddy IP allowlist /
etc). `/metrics` itself bypasses the metrics middleware to avoid
recording every scrape into the request-counter series, which
would inflate cardinality and mostly measure Prometheus's own
scrape interval.

Readiness probe — distinct from `/health`, which only confirms
the process is running. `/ready` returns 200 once the service
has finished startup work (notably `rehydrate()` on the on-disk
backend); 503 before that.

PATCH semantics — partial-update of the edge's property map. The
underlying storage call is `merge_edge_properties`. This mirrors
node CRUD's PUT (REPLACE) shape but with the verb flipped to match
the storage primitive's asymmetry — see `replace_node_properties`
docs for why nodes don't have a merge primitive.

put.summary:
PUT semantics — full replacement of the node's property map (the
underlying storage call is `replace_node_properties`). PATCH is
not exposed because there is no merge primitive on nodes; if a
caller needs partial-update semantics they GET, mutate, PUT.
put.description:
An empty or omitted `properties` (`{}`) is a deliberate full wipe —
PUT replaces the whole map, so `{}` clears every property. This is
the REST-correct reading of PUT and is intentionally NOT rejected;
callers that don't mean to clear should send the properties they
want to keep (or use the GET-mutate-PUT cycle above).

AlgoDirection.description: Whether edges are treated as one-way or symmetric.

AlgoScope.description:
Subgraph selection shared by every algorithm. Omitted fields mean "all":
no `node_types` => every node type in the schema; no `edge_types` => every
edge type.

edge_types.description: Edge types to include. Omit for all types.

node_types.description: Node types to include. Omit for all types.

BatchOp.description:
One mutation. Field names match the existing single-handler bodies
so callers can translate `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/nodes` payloads into
`{"op": "create_node", ...}` entries with no field renames.

BatchOpError.description:
Structured per-op error body. Plain-text errors (the convention for
single handlers) lose the index of the failing op, which is the one
thing a batch caller needs to diagnose a rejection.

BetweennessRequest.description:
Request for `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/algo/betweenness`. Edge weights are path
**costs** and must be strictly positive; omit `weight` for unit-cost
distances.

normalized.description: Normalize scores by the number of node pairs. Defaults to true.

ClosenessRequest.description:
Request for `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/algo/closeness`. Edge weights are path
**costs** (higher = farther) and must be strictly positive; omit `weight`
for unit-cost (hop-count) distances. On a `directed` graph this is *outward*
closeness (distances from each node to the rest, following edge direction).

ClusteringResponse.description:
Response for `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/algo/clustering` (undirected). Per-node
local clustering scores plus the two global summaries.

average_clustering.description: Mean local clustering coefficient over all nodes.

scores.description: Local clustering coefficient per node, highest first.

oneOf.description:
Present only when `resolve_target = true` AND the target node
was found. Caller can rely on `target.is_some()` ↔ resolution
succeeded; absence with `resolve_target = true` means the edge
points at a node id no schema-candidate type could find — a
referential-integrity gap worth surfacing in caller logs (see
the v0.5.1 batch.rs hazard documentation for one source of such
orphans).

ComponentsResponse.description:
One (weakly-)connected component: the node ids it contains. Also the response
shape for strongly-connected components (`/algo/scc`).

components.description:
Components as lists of node ids; each list sorted, and the lists ordered
deterministically by their smallest id.

CutEdge.description:
One bridge (cut edge), as the unordered pair of node ids it connects
(`a < b`).

CutsResponse.description: Articulation points and bridges of the (undirected) subgraph.

articulation_points.description: Node ids whose removal increases the number of connected components.

bridges.description: Edges whose removal increases the number of connected components.

DegreeModeWire.description:
Which incident edges degree centrality counts. For an undirected graph all
three read the same symmetric adjacency.

oneOf.description:
Edge-weight projection. When present, scores are weighted degree
(strength); when absent, scores are plain incident-edge counts.

limit.description:
Cap on the total edges returned (outgoing + incoming combined).
Optional and defaults to `MAX_LIMIT` — unlike the *required*
`limit` on `edges:collect` / `nodes:scan`, because this route
shipped without one and defaulting keeps existing callers
(which send no `limit`) working while still bounding the
super-node response.

truncated.description:
`true` when more edges existed than `limit` allowed — some were
omitted from `edges`.

EdgesCollectResponse.description:
Untagged so the JSON has the shape the caller asked for: an
`{"edges": [...], "truncated": ...}` object for `format = "edges"`,
an `{"adjacency": {...}, "truncated": ...}` object for
`format = "adjacency"`. Caller distinguishes by which field is
present (always exactly one).

EigenvectorRequest.description:
Request for `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/algo/eigenvector`. Edge weights are
**strengths**; omit `weight` for an unweighted run.

Eigenvector centrality is computed on the **undirected** graph (it is only
well-defined there). `direction` therefore accepts only `undirected` (the
default); `directed` is rejected with a 400 pointing to `/algo/pagerank`,
which is the directed importance measure.

max_iterations.description: Iteration budget before a non-convergence error. Defaults to 100.

FlowEdge.description:
One min-cut edge crossing from the source side to the sink side. For an
undirected graph `from` is always the source-side endpoint (there is no
stored edge direction).

LinkPredictionMethodWire.description: Which neighborhood-overlap score link prediction uses.

LinkPredictionRequest.description:
Request for `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/algo/link_prediction`. Treats the subgraph
as undirected. With `source`, predicts links from that node; without it,
across all non-adjacent pairs. Results are ranked by score and capped.

limit.description: Max ranked results. Defaults to 100, capped at the standard result limit.

source.description: Predict links from this node only; omit for all non-adjacent pairs.

MatrixResponse.description: An N×N result matrix (row-major), e.g. a pairwise similarity/distance matrix.

MaxFlowResponse.description:
Response for `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/algo/max_flow`. The max flow value equals
the min-cut capacity; `source_side` is the node partition on the source side
of that cut, and `cut_edges` the crossing edges.

NodeListResponse.description:
Envelope for node-list endpoints. Matches the convention used by
`GraphListResponse` (`{graphs: [...]}`) — a top-level object, not a
bare array, so future additions (pagination cursor, total count)
are non-breaking.

NodesScanResponse.description:
Untagged so the wire produces either `{"results": ["id", ...], ...}`
or `{"results": [{...node}, ...], ...}` depending on `return`. The
node shape is the shared `NodeResponse` — same `{node_type,
node_id, properties}` triple `GET /nodes` and the rest of foundation
emit, so consumers can deserialize into a single struct.

PageRankRequest.description:
Request for `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/algo/pagerank`. Edge weights are
**strengths** (a node splits its rank among out-edges in proportion to
weight); omit `weight` for an unweighted (equal-split) run.

max_iterations.description: Iteration budget before a non-convergence error. Defaults to 100.

PairwiseDistanceRequest.description: A set of equal-length vectors plus a metric (for `pairwise_distance`).

PersonalizedPageRankRequest.description:
Request for `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/algo/personalized_pagerank` (random walk
with restart). Like PageRank, but teleport mass returns to `seeds`, so scores
measure relevance to that seed set. Edge weights are **strengths**.

max_iterations.description: Iteration budget before a non-convergence error. Defaults to 100.

seeds.description: Seed node ids the walk restarts to. Required (non-empty).

PowerRequest.description: A vector plus a scalar exponent (for `elementwise_power`).

Precision.description:
Numeric precision for vector ops. Wire form is the lowercase
variant name (`"f32"` / `"f64"`). Public so `dynograph-client`
can re-export it and consumers can pass `Precision::F32` instead
of stringly-typed `"f32"`.

PredictedLink.description:
One predicted (currently-absent) link and its score. `a`/`b` are the endpoint
node ids (for a single-source request, `a` is the source).

SampleRequest.description:
A sample of values for a descriptive statistic (f64-only — no
`precision`). Named `values` rather than `v` to read as a sample,
not a geometric vector.

ScaleRequest.description: A vector plus a scalar coefficient (for `scale`).

ScopedRequest.description:
A request that carries only a subgraph `scope` — shared by the purely
structural algorithms (`/algo/components`, `/algo/cuts`, `/algo/scc`), which
take no weights or direction.

ScoresResponse.description:
Per-node centrality scores, highest first (ties broken by node id). Shared by
every score-producing algorithm (degree, PageRank, eigenvector, closeness,
betweenness, personalized PageRank).

limit.description: Max hits to return (1..=MAX_LIMIT). Defaults to 10.

node_type.description: Optional node-type filter; omit to search all types in the graph.

query.description:
Raw keyword query. Tokenized with the index analyzer and matched as a
conjunction (every token must occur). Punctuation and `field:value`
input are treated as plain text, not query syntax.

ShortestPathResponse.description:
A shortest path between two nodes. `found` is false (with an empty `path`)
when the target is unreachable from the source.

distance.description: Total path cost (hop count when unweighted); 0 when not found.

path.description: Node ids in order, source first and target last; empty when not found.

SourceTargetRequest.description:
A request carrying a `source`/`target` node pair plus the usual scope, weight,
and direction — shared by `/algo/shortest_path` (weight = path cost) and
`/algo/max_flow` (weight = capacity). The two `source`/`target` ids are
required; the per-endpoint weight semantics are documented on each route.

SourceTypeFilter.description:
Source-type matcher. Untagged so the JSON can be either a string
(`"*"` or a single type name) or an array of names.

ToposortResponse.description:
Response for `POST /v1/graphs/{id}/algo/toposort` (directed). `acyclic` is
true for a DAG, with `order` a topological ordering; otherwise `order` is
empty (the graph has a cycle).

TraversedNode.description:
Per-result entry. `properties` is populated only when
`return: "nodes"`; for `return: "ids"` the field is omitted from
the wire shape via `skip_serializing_if`. Caller distinguishes by
presence of the field, OR by request echo (the request shape is
the source of truth for which they asked for).

VectorsRequest.description: A set of equal-length vectors (for `centroid` and `pairwise_cosine`).

WeightSpec.description:
Edge-weight projection. With neither field set, edges are unweighted (every
weight is `1.0`). `property` takes precedence over `edge_type_weights` if
both are given.

edge_type_weights.description:
Per-edge-type constant weights. An in-scope edge whose type is absent
from this map is a 400.

property.description:
Read this numeric edge property as the weight. Missing or non-numeric on
any in-scope edge is a 400 (fail loud).
